sylvia: Heads up — onboarding and a few internal samples started failing after the exports tidy in @redwood/sdk@0.8.0. Repro uses older CI image (Node 14) and Cloudflare Workers.

igor: Paste the error?

sylvia: Worker emulation shows: ```Error: The requested module '@redwood/sdk' does not provide an export named 'default' at file:///workspace/examples/onboard/worker.mjs:2:1```

max: On Node 14 + Jest the failing stack is `TypeError: require('@redwood/sdk').default is undefined` from examples/setup.js. Seems we removed the CJS entry in package `exports`.

tia: Our index.d.ts still declares a default export which makes TS users do `import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk'` — so there's a type/runtime mismatch. That explains the onboarding confusion.

igor: We intentionally moved to ESM-first and removed `main`/legacy CJS. But some things rely on `sdk.default` shape (auth retry middleware, integration fixtures). We need a compatibility shim.

sylvia: Quick mitigation I've added to the onboarding README: use named import or this require fallback:```// ESM prefered
import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk'
// CJS fallback for old CI
const sdk = require('@redwood/sdk').default || require('@redwood/sdk')```

max: For a proper patch I'd add an explicit CJS require entrypoint in exports: "\." : { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./cjs/index.js" } and ship `cjs/index.js` that re-exports the ESM build while preserving default and named shapes.

tia: Also add a tiny `types/cjs.d.ts` that keeps `export default` so `import Redwood from` keeps type-checking. That avoids noisy TS errors for new users.

igor: Watch out — pnpm/bun/deno pack semantics differ. Our pack step removed the require path entirely which produced an ESM-only tarball for some consumers. We should validate generated tarball in release CI.

sylvia: Agreed. Proposed CI additions: run `node -e \"console.log(require('./package'))\"` against the packed tarball, run an ESM import smoke (`node --input-type=module -e \"import('@redwood/sdk').then(()=>console.log('esm ok'))\"`), and run a headless worker import via wrangler or worker emulation. Filed ISSUE-1355.

max: I opened PR #4382 — adds `exports.\".\"` require/import entries, `cjs/index.js` shim with:```const esm = require('../dist/esm');const root = esm && esm.default ? esm.default : esm; Object.assign(root, esm); module.exports = root;```Also includes `types/cjs.d.ts` and a changelog note about ESM-first with compat shim.

tia: We should also run the auth/retry integration matrix before cutting patch. Some middleware expects `sdk.default.auth.retry` to exist. If the cjs shim returns a flattened object we keep compatibility.

pkg-bot: publish-bot: Canary @redwood/sdk@0.8.1-canary.0 published for validation.

ci-bot: ci: running samples matrix (Node 12/14/16, Bun, Cloudflare worker emulation, auth integration) against canary.

igor: One more note — update onboarding docs to show both `import * as Redwood from '@redwood/sdk'` and `import { createClient }` patterns and add a short paragraph explaining why default vs named matters across runtimes.

sylvia: After canary verification I'll swap examples to the safer named imports and land the compat patch. We should also add a release checklist item: \"validate package exports for require/import + worker import\" to avoid future regressions.

max: Running full auth matrix now. If green I'll merge and cut 0.8.1 patch. Thanks all for the quick turnaround. :rocket:
